title: Why it is so easy to float in the Dead Sea
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do people float in the Dead Sea?
Is it easier to float in salt water?
Why do I sink when I breathe out?

explain.say: Whether you float depends on density, how much mass is packed into each bit of space. With your lungs full of air, your body is about as dense as fresh water, so you only just float.

explain.say: The Dead Sea, between Israel and Jordan, is about ten times saltier than the ocean, around 34 percent salt. Its water is so dense that the upthrust holds you high, like lying on a bed.

items.ask: Why is the Dead Sea so salty?

explain.say: You float when you push aside your own weight of water. Denser water weighs more, so less of you needs to be under the surface, and in the Dead Sea about a fifth of your body stays above it.

faq.q: Why is the Dead Sea so salty?
faq.a: It lies in the lowest land on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level, and no river flows out of it. Water only leaves by evaporating in the hot sun, leaving its salt behind, so the salt has built up over thousands of years.
asks: How salty is the Dead Sea?

faq.a: Density is how much mass is packed into a given space. A cubic metre of fresh water has a mass of about 1,000 kilograms; anything less dense than the liquid it is in will float.
asks: Why do some things float and others sink?

faq.q: Why is floating easier in the sea than in a pool?
faq.a: Salt makes sea water denser, about 1,025 kilograms per cubic metre against 1,000 for fresh water. Denser water gives a stronger upthrust for the same amount of you underwater, so you float a little higher.
asks: Do you float better in salt water?

faq.q: Can you swim in the Dead Sea?
faq.a: You float so high that swimming normally is awkward, so most people just lie back. Visitors must keep the very salty water out of their eyes and mouth, because it stings and is harmful to swallow.
asks: Can you sink in the Dead Sea?

faq.q: Why do you float better with full lungs?
faq.a: Air in your lungs makes your body less dense overall. Breathe out fully and many people slowly sink, even in a pool.
asks: Why do I sink when I breathe out?

facts: The Dead Sea's water is about 34 percent salt, nearly ten times saltier than the ocean.
The Dead Sea's surface lies about 430 metres below sea level, the lowest land on Earth.
Dead Sea water has a density of about 1.24 kilograms per litre.
